summary: Libenge territory (Sud-Ubangi) lies along the Ubangi river facing the Central African Republic, far from the eastern conflict zones. No Congolese or foreign armed group is known to hold territory here; Libenge town, the territorial seat, hosts the territorial administration, PNC commissariat, ANR, DGM border services and an FARDC presence watching the CAR border. The Boyabu camp area hosts Central African refugees under UNHCR/CNR management with a PNC security detachment. Rural villages in the Libenge and Mawuya health zones fall under PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs; insecurity is limited to ordinary crime, occasional cross-border spillover and customary disputes. No recent sources could be retrieved in this run (web search budget exhausted, ReliefWeb blocked). The assessment therefore rests on default state presence.
